note: Storyboard test, 14 Nov 2026: Book the First of A Tale of Two Cities, twelve beats drawn by Gemini from the text alone. No reference images and no Midjourney: every picture is new. Second pass: the six beats the first run missed.
style: An oil painting in the manner of nineteenth-century academic history painting: rich palette, dramatic chiaroscuro, visible brushwork, painterly and cinematic, 16:9. England and France in 1775: tricorn hats, greatcoats, knee-breeches, buckled shoes, candle and lantern light, no modern objects. No captions, no signature, no frames, no black bars or borders.

people.lorry: Mr. Jarvis Lorry: a neat, orderly English banker of about sixty, clean-shaven, a small sleek crisp flaxen wig close to his head, a well-worn brown suit and waistcoat, brown stockings, plain buckled shoes, white linen
people.lucie: Lucie Manette: a young lady of seventeen, short, slight and pretty, with a quantity of golden hair and blue eyes, a smooth young forehead that lifts in an intent, inquiring expression
people.pross: Miss Pross: a tall, strong, red-faced Englishwoman with red hair, in an odd tight-fitting dress and an enormous tall bonnet
people.defarge: Ernest Defarge: a bull-necked, martial-looking Frenchman of thirty with crisply curling short dark hair, shirtsleeves rolled to the elbow, bare brown arms, good bold eyes
people.madame: Madame Defarge: a stout Frenchwoman of thirty, steady face, strong features, darkly defined eyebrows, watchful eye, a large hand heavily ringed, wrapped in fur with a bright shawl about her head, large earrings, knitting
people.manette: Doctor Manette: a gaunt old man worn by eighteen years in prison, a ragged white beard, hollow face, exceedingly bright eyes under dark eyebrows, confused white hair, ragged shirt

beats.text: A narrow grey Paris street in 1775: a tall gaunt man in a long ragged nightcap, his mouth stained red with spilled wine, reaches up and scrawls a single large word in dark red wine on a pale stone wall with his fingertip; ragged men and women behind him gather spilled wine from the cobbles around a broken cask. A grim, quiet moment.
